# There is no Denmark

*Generated by `scripts/pages/areas.py` from `data/derived/areas.json`, `data/derived/synchrony.json` and `data/derived/livestock_baskets.json`.*

## Water bodies are management units

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-UNITS">**The [123](SOURCES.md#F-2f37b30ded) marine water bodies are management units.** They exist so that an authority can be made responsible for an area of sea and given a target for it. Nothing in the data discovered them, and a number computed per water body is a number about the administration until something shows otherwise.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-UNITS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-AGG">The national argument is made in aggregates: one land-borne load, and one share of it for agriculture - [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% in the figure DANVA cites from Miljøstyrelsen and Aarhus University. Aggregation is where the information goes: a figure true of Denmark need not hold for any one water body inside it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-AGG "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### Two meanings of "a body of water", and the switch between them

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ENCLOSURE">"Roskilde Fjord" is not an arbitrary line on a map, and it is worth saying so plainly before objecting to anything. It names a real hydrographic object: an inlet bounded by land that opens to the sea through Isefjorden. That is a **claim about enclosure**, it is physical, and it is true.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ENCLOSURE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-HOMOGENEITY">The assessment then uses the same word to mean something else entirely: that a measurement taken anywhere in it stands for the whole of it. That is a **claim about homogeneity**, and it is statistical. One sense is about where the water is bounded; the other is about whether the water inside those bounds is alike. Nothing carries you from the first to the second, and the name does the carrying unnoticed because the same three words serve both.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-HOMOGENEITY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-PHYSICS">**And where exchange is restricted, the physics runs against the transfer, not with it.** Restricted exchange is what *preserves* a gradient. A basin with freshwater entering at its head and little exchange at its mouth holds salinity, residence-time and oxygen gradients along its length because it does not flush; open water erases such differences by mixing. So the better the enclosure, the weaker the homogeneity assumption becomes: the two senses **pull in opposite directions**, and the enclosures that most deserve their names are the ones least entitled to be treated as single units.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-PHYSICS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-TWO-UNITS">The partition half-concedes this without following it through. Roskilde Fjord appears here as two water bodies, `DKCOAST1` (ydre, [71](SOURCES.md#F-1e2174d480) km²) and `DKCOAST2` (indre, [52](SOURCES.md#F-721904d9f2) km²) — an admission that one enclosure is at least two units.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-TWO-UNITS "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-SPLIT-UNSTATED">The documents this project holds give the general basis for water bodies' boundaries — the water framework directive asks member states to set them, and the plans sort coastal waters into types with a catchment each — but none of them says why this fjord is two units rather than one or three, or what measurement would settle it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SPLIT-UNSTATED "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-X22">A boundary drawn inside a fjord is a hypothesis about where the water changes, and it can be tested: `X22` in [EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md) sets out how, using pairs of measurements at matched separation either side of a line.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-X22 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-POSITION">The practical rule that follows, and the reason the station-level series exist: **the unit of observation is a position.** Everything else — this page included — is an aggregate computed inside somebody's polygon, and should be read as a statement about that polygon as much as about the sea.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-POSITION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The switch, measured in the fjord it is named after

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ROSK-METHOD">The station-level series make this checkable rather than arguable. Both halves of Roskilde Fjord carry several stations, so for any month where [3](SOURCES.md#F-47737412fa) or more measured, the disagreement *between* stations can be set against the variation *across* months. *Spread between stations* is the population standard deviation across the stations in a month, averaged over the months, beside the median range; *spread across months* is the standard deviation of the monthly means.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ROSK-METHOD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ILTSVIND">In Denmark, oxygen below [4](SOURCES.md#F-6f707414ef) mg/L is called iltsvind.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ILTSVIND "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ROSK-OXY">**The inner fjord's own stations disagree about bottom oxygen by a median of [3.35](SOURCES.md#F-9f772be675) mg/l within a single month.** A spread that size is most of the distance from zero to that threshold, so in a month when the fjord's bottom water is near it, one station can read below and another above — and whether that body "has iltsvind" can then depend on which of its own stations is read. The ratio puts it another way: the spread between stations is **[65](SOURCES.md#F-fd09d07246)% of the spread of the monthly means across months**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ROSK-OXY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ROSK-HALVES">**And the two halves fail on different variables.** The inner fjord's stations disagree for oxygen ([0.65](SOURCES.md#F-fbcf0ce589)) and agree for salinity ([0.29](SOURCES.md#F-791801daea)); the outer fjord's are the reverse — close for oxygen ([0.25](SOURCES.md#F-3c4eacfb1c)), apart for salinity ([0.87](SOURCES.md#F-934bf566cd)). Within this one fjord, a boundary drawn to serve one variable does not serve the other. That is one case, not a proof about every partition; it is the case `X22` would test systematically.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ROSK-HALVES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What the stations' own behaviour supports

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-SYNC-METHOD">Only moving together over time is tested here, never similar levels. Each station's own seasonal cycle is removed - its median for each calendar month - and each pair of stations is compared month by month on what is left (Kendall's tau). Chance is one station's series shifted against the other's by whole years, which keeps each series intact and breaks only the tie in time. A pair moves together beyond chance when it beats its shifted copies at the [5](SOURCES.md#F-3b2d20330e)% level, so that share of pairs passes by chance alone. Distances are straight lines between stations; land is ignored.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-SYNC-METHOD "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-SYNC-THIN">For bed oxygen, [15,630](SOURCES.md#F-8350a1fecc) pairs of stations share a window long enough for the test, involving [215](SOURCES.md#F-a86ec435c5) stations; another [16,394](SOURCES.md#F-ebca1e975e) pairs overlap too briefly to be shifted, and are left undecided.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-SYNC-THIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-NEAR-FAR">**Stations near each other move together far more often than stations far apart.** Of the [515](SOURCES.md#F-0028df42f4) bed-oxygen pairs less than [20](SOURCES.md#F-07cd695a12) km apart, [80.8](SOURCES.md#F-ac53144651)% move together beyond chance; of the [15,115](SOURCES.md#F-5d944a6f3d) pairs farther apart, [32.3](SOURCES.md#F-945efa0a7b)%.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-NEAR-FAR "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-MATCHED">**At the same distance apart, pairs inside one water body move together more often than pairs across a line.** For bed oxygen, the share moving together beyond chance is higher inside by [12.3](SOURCES.md#F-10787db0ef) percentage points, pooled over distance bins (standard error [4.2](SOURCES.md#F-eb140fce5f), leaving out one water body at a time). With finer bins the gain is [9.4](SOURCES.md#F-d3b1b1a9a6) points: part of it was distance left over inside the bins.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-MATCHED "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-WATER-MASSES">**But bed salinity, which says nothing about an ailment, gains about as much** - [10.7](SOURCES.md#F-268791d534) points (standard error [5.1](SOURCES.md#F-82dd852570)) - and in the average size of the co-movement it gains more than oxygen: a tau [0.148](SOURCES.md#F-156fbb13cd) higher inside, against [0.096](SOURCES.md#F-535ce55740) for oxygen. So the lines follow differences in the water itself, the kind a sill or a fjord mouth makes, and the oxygen gain is no larger than the water's. Nothing here shows a shared ailment on top of shared water.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-WATER-MASSES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-SAME-DAY">**Part of that could be the sampling trip.** Stations in one water body share a sampling day in [75.8](SOURCES.md#F-e2deeefc59)% of their pair-months for bed oxygen, pairs across a line in [24.5](SOURCES.md#F-e56bd665f5)%. On months the two stations were sampled on different days, same-body pairs still move together more often than pairs across a line at the same distance - by [21.3](SOURCES.md#F-3fd7547b48) percentage points for oxygen (standard error [10.1](SOURCES.md#F-c9991de63b)) and [15.2](SOURCES.md#F-5b2ee30ac8) for salinity (standard error [5.3](SOURCES.md#F-e7ba718071)). The gain persists, but for oxygen it now rests on [48](SOURCES.md#F-29807014de) same-body pairs, where the full test had [229](SOURCES.md#F-9cf5db7d4a). With samples at least [5](SOURCES.md#F-27e9fb02ee) days apart, only [10](SOURCES.md#F-5d2beae577) same-body oxygen pairs remain: too few to answer.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-SAME-DAY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-OWN-GROUPS">**The groups the stations draw for themselves do not follow the lines.** Joining every pair that moves together beyond chance links [215](SOURCES.md#F-8d30be2804) of the [215](SOURCES.md#F-a16bc60f71) tested oxygen stations into one group. Split into communities by the strength of their co-movement (Louvain), they form [5](SOURCES.md#F-563f40a9d6) groups, each spanning between [5](SOURCES.md#F-ffd9266804) and [58](SOURCES.md#F-814d269e42) water bodies; [0](SOURCES.md#F-3b6385747d) of them form a contiguous patch of sea. Of the [44](SOURCES.md#F-7114aae485) water bodies with two or more tested stations, [15](SOURCES.md#F-5f316e5b67) are split between groups. And the groups partly sort by when their stations were measured: one group's records end, at the median, in [2014](SOURCES.md#F-871e13a63c), the largest group's in [2026](SOURCES.md#F-12b934b105).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-OWN-GROUPS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-NATIONAL">**And distance does not end it.** [32.3](SOURCES.md#F-945efa0a7b)% of bed-oxygen pairs [20](SOURCES.md#F-07cd695a12) km or more apart move together beyond chance, where chance alone gives [5](SOURCES.md#F-3b2d20330e)%. With each station's own yearly level also removed, [30.1](SOURCES.md#F-f185d8eb8f)% still do; on months the two were sampled on different days, [29.9](SOURCES.md#F-b6a42a3593)%. What moves stations everywhere at once is common to the whole population: a national signal, not a property of any place in it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-NATIONAL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-WEATHER">Shared weather is the obvious candidate; it is not tested here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-WEATHER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Are the stations alike?

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-READINGS">A grouping that does no better than random baskets has two readings. The grouping may be bad; or the stations may be alike, so that no grouping could do better and treating them as one kind drops nothing that matters. One comparison decides between them: the spread among stations against the spread of one station measured again.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-READINGS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-ALIKE">For summer bed oxygen, one station changes by a median of [1.00](SOURCES.md#F-5715a4bf95) mg/l from one summer month to the next - more than its measurement noise alone, since that includes real change within a summer. Two stations in the same water body, in the same month, differ by [1.01](SOURCES.md#F-9934e73a43): about as much. Any two stations differ by [1.85](SOURCES.md#F-60aeacd796). And the stations' own summer medians spread over an interquartile range of [2.27](SOURCES.md#F-62495bc121) mg/l, where shuffling which station measured what, among the stations measured in the same month, gives [0.65](SOURCES.md#F-2f8f0105e8); [0](SOURCES.md#F-a8ba92472b) of [500](SOURCES.md#F-60fb865592) shuffles reached the real spread.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-ALIKE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-READING-A">**So the stations are not one kind.** They differ beyond a station's own month-to-month change, and the differences sit between water bodies rather than within them. That is the first reading: the population is not uniform, and a grouping has to explain the differences between water bodies - which, for livestock, the next section shows it does not. Oxygen saturation gives the same answer.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-READING-A "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## A grouping along a causal line: livestock

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-NAIVE">Stations are grouped here by the livestock on the land that drains to their water body: the first basket drawn along a causal line, and **a naive one**. The livestock is where herds are registered, in the 2024 register, not where their manure is spread, counted in the regulatory unit DE rather than as nitrogen, against station records that span decades. Each catchment is linked to the water body it touches along the coast, a link built here, and an outer fjord does not inherit its inner fjord's land. And low-livestock land is not low-load land: urban and sewage loads are not in this grouping. Livestock figures on this page are totals over areas of land, never a single farm.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-NAIVE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-ABSENT">**Where livestock is near-absent was set before looking:** a catchment with less than [20](SOURCES.md#F-c3b0d186bb)% of the national density of [57.2](SOURCES.md#F-1001dc7a5c) DE per km², that is below [11.4](SOURCES.md#F-b525193686). [17](SOURCES.md#F-065ff768af) catchments meet it. The largest of them, from [377](SOURCES.md#F-a4697d53ad) to [874](SOURCES.md#F-3fb2e0a13e) km² of land, are in north-east Zealand, around and north of Copenhagen: Køge Bugt; Roskilde Fjord, ydre; Nordlige Øresund; Roskilde Fjord, indre; Kattegat, Nordsjælland. The rest are small, none over [118](SOURCES.md#F-bfcb797d8c) km²: islands, nors, and small fjords and bays.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-ABSENT "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-BASKETS">Every station in a water body that land drains to, with at least [4](SOURCES.md#F-29d6cc5359) summer months of bed oxygen, enters a basket: thirds of the stations by the density of the land behind their water body - low up to [27.7](SOURCES.md#F-cf4618bdfe) DE per km², high above [54.8](SOURCES.md#F-c7f3456ff6) - with the near-absent end inside the low third. That is [643](SOURCES.md#F-b9535433e0) stations in [105](SOURCES.md#F-e25ec7e41e) water bodies; [69](SOURCES.md#F-9c22f0162b) of them sit in the [16](SOURCES.md#F-7d586bd238) near-absent water bodies.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-BASKETS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-LEVELS">**Summer bed oxygen barely differs in the middle:** the heavy basket's median station is [0.23](SOURCES.md#F-71e860dfb1) mg/l below the low basket's. The difference is in the low tail: the heavy basket's tenth percentile is [3.10](SOURCES.md#F-da907f9a64) mg/l, the low basket's [5.13](SOURCES.md#F-f495d52af7).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-LEVELS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-FLOOR">**Counted as independent stations, livestock looks strong.** The near-absent basket's median station has [0.77](SOURCES.md#F-836559ed99) mg/l more bed oxygen than the heavy basket's, and [0](SOURCES.md#F-615a188d4a) of [10,000](SOURCES.md#F-b587604f8e) random baskets of the same sizes reached that. But the [643](SOURCES.md#F-b9535433e0) stations sit in only [105](SOURCES.md#F-e25ec7e41e) water bodies and move with them. Shuffling the densities between whole water bodies instead, each keeping its stations together, puts every contrast inside the central [95](SOURCES.md#F-8503421679)% of the random results: [656](SOURCES.md#F-8081f0ed9a) of [10,000](SOURCES.md#F-9624a1ccda) draws gave a near-absent lead at least as large. **For bed oxygen the livestock line does not beat the noise floor.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-FLOOR "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-NOTHING">Nor does the basket add to the difference between stations: two stations in different water bodies, in the same month, differ by [1.90](SOURCES.md#F-c6b52bc4e5) mg/l when they share a basket and [1.85](SOURCES.md#F-68eda10e83) when they do not.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-NOTHING "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-UBIQ">What every random basket shows is common to all the stations, whatever the membership: bed oxygen bottoms out in August in [3,000](SOURCES.md#F-40118d852e) of [3,000](SOURCES.md#F-138a08a633) random baskets, and in the real ones. Only the heavy basket's low tail is unusual: its tenth percentile, [3.10](SOURCES.md#F-18233556b3) mg/l, is near the lowest any random basket of its size gave, [3.04](SOURCES.md#F-b937c262dd).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-UBIQ "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-STRATA">**Within strata, cut before looking at a bed salinity of [20](SOURCES.md#F-e01ce40d1f)‰ and a depth of [10](SOURCES.md#F-34dd0a10bb) m,** the heavy basket's median falls further below the low basket's: in brackish water by [0.75](SOURCES.md#F-2d630874ba) mg/l, in shallow water by [0.56](SOURCES.md#F-8bf5caa91a), in deep brackish water by [2.12](SOURCES.md#F-8134a06ef9). There it reaches the edge of the water-body random band - outside its central [95](SOURCES.md#F-8503421679)%, inside its full range - and never clearly past it. In salty bottom water it reverses: the heavy basket's median is [0.97](SOURCES.md#F-b46b22e0f0) mg/l above the low one's. Using only summers from [2010](SOURCES.md#F-4a7f758f04), closer to the 2024 register, the gap shrinks to [0.14](SOURCES.md#F-a4bf90a242) mg/l.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-STRATA "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-SALTY">A reading, not tested here: in salty bottom water oxygen is set more by the layering of the water and by inflow than by the land nearby.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-SALTY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-DOES">**What this shows, and what it does not.** Heavy-livestock water has the worse low tail. Heavy-livestock land does not mean low oxygen everywhere: Ringkøbing Fjord has [76](SOURCES.md#F-2552d27913) DE per km² behind it and a median summer bed oxygen of [9.25](SOURCES.md#F-9343e08642) mg/l across its stations, above the [7.80](SOURCES.md#F-252b5c0f8e) of all basketed stations. It does not show that livestock lowers bed oxygen: it compares levels, and similar levels are not a shared cause. The test of one is whether stations move together along the line, and that has not yet been run for livestock.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-DOES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-FLUO">**Fluorescence is the one measure the livestock baskets separate clearly.** The heavy basket's median station reads [3.90](SOURCES.md#F-a47be7eb8f), the low basket's [1.39](SOURCES.md#F-37626a308d); a heavy station reads below a low one in [11](SOURCES.md#F-7c295b84b0)% of pairs; and the contrast lies outside the whole range of both kinds of random basket.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-FLUO "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-LS-FLUO-CAVEAT">It carries a caveat nobody has checked: the panel's fluorescence is a whole-cast value in relative units, so a difference between instruments or monitoring programmes could produce the same separation.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-LS-FLUO-CAVEAT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Water-body numbers, where a management question needs them

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-ADMIN">**The numbers in this section are administrative:** counts of management units, and what stands behind the targets they are given - not findings about the sea.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-ADMIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The state of knowledge, counted

| | areas | km² | share of sea |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All marine water bodies in the national marine layer | [123](SOURCES.md#F-2f37b30ded) | [43,579](SOURCES.md#F-661cd6785e) | [100.0](SOURCES.md#F-7006a6fba5)% |
| …with a DHI statistical model (see below) | [25](SOURCES.md#F-93bddbb930) | [4,834](SOURCES.md#F-62228ab3b0) | [11.1](SOURCES.md#F-e0d1926291)% |
| …with bathing-water stations, repeated over years | [70](SOURCES.md#F-4d2ae5aa40) | [17,900](SOURCES.md#F-a525025154) | [41.1](SOURCES.md#F-17ca3ee060)% |
| …with three or more informative bathing stations | [43](SOURCES.md#F-af660690f5) | [15,818](SOURCES.md#F-3dd92a2b2b) | [36.3](SOURCES.md#F-adaaf683db)% |
| …with neither the flag nor a bathing station | [46](SOURCES.md#F-5f06ac0dbc) | [24,359](SOURCES.md#F-a981c481ca) | [55.9](SOURCES.md#F-e1ba4b224c)% |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-MODEL-MATCH">**The model flag follows DHI's list.** A water body counts as modelled when DHI's 2015 method report lists it among the water bodies with a station-level statistical model, matched to this layer by DHI's water-body number, with every name read against the layer's own (`data/manual/statistical_models.json`). One of DHI's models covers five Limfjord bredninger together, so all five are counted; one water body it lists, Randers Fjord's Grund Fjord, is not in the marine layer used here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-MODEL-MATCH "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-NEITHER">Counted with that flag, [46](SOURCES.md#F-5f06ac0dbc) water bodies covering [24,359](SOURCES.md#F-a981c481ca) km² ([56](SOURCES.md#F-e1ba4b224c)% of Danish sea) carry neither the flag nor a repeated observation **in the two layers counted here** — bathing water, and the hazardous-substance layer, which holds no marine point.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-NEITHER "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-REQUIREMENT">A requirement does not wait for either: in the method behind the second water plans, every one of its [119](SOURCES.md#F-3b74139141) water bodies was given an indsatsbehov, whether it had a statistical model or not.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-REQUIREMENT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### What an absence can be counted over

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-ABSENCE-RULE">**A claim of absence is only as wide as the search behind it**, and this search was two layers deep.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ABSENCE-RULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-REGISTER">ODA's station register holds **[6,258](SOURCES.md#F-f2f5d986a1) positioned marine stations**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-REGISTER "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-SERIES-COVERAGE">The part of it this page can place in water bodies is the station series behind the co-movement tests and the livestock baskets above — [1,415](SOURCES.md#F-5fb04be1c0) stations with a monthly record, [1,313](SOURCES.md#F-8a40ae1f65) of them inside a water body by point in polygon — and **[119](SOURCES.md#F-481802d78d) of the [123](SOURCES.md#F-4cb4902088) water bodies contain at least one of those.** Counted over that series: [4](SOURCES.md#F-9552070f3a) water bodies contain no station with data in [2](SOURCES.md#F-3fca6d1b99) or more distinct years, [10](SOURCES.md#F-335ad5024c) water bodies contain no station with data in [5](SOURCES.md#F-4549390408) or more distinct years, [12](SOURCES.md#F-4ad752eb92) water bodies contain no station with data in [10](SOURCES.md#F-e17184bafe) or more distinct years.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-SERIES-COVERAGE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-NOT-PERCENT">**Those are counts, and they are deliberately not percentages.** Saying *[8](SOURCES.md#F-f02c7ae231)% of the sea has no long observation* would be the missing-denominator error this project exists to point at. The denominator is known — the sea is [43,579](SOURCES.md#F-655cb351e2) km². The numerator is not, because it is the extent of an absence, and an absence can only be measured against a search that was exhaustive. Ours was ODA plus two layers; ICES and EMODnet sit outside it, and so does whatever university, municipal or unpublished series exist.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-NOT-PERCENT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

The test is whether **the category named is the same width as the corpus searched.**

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-SAME-WIDTH">**Same width — an exact statement is fine, including of an absence.** *None of the [123](SOURCES.md#F-2f37b30ded) water bodies has a marine point in the national hazardous-substance layer: its [256](SOURCES.md#F-9edac16b2c) points are [152](SOURCES.md#F-076f9f4115) lake and [104](SOURCES.md#F-0b7a823dec) river.* The category is that layer and the count is of all of it, so its complement is exact.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SAME-WIDTH "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-WIDER">**Category wider than corpus — only a count is honest.** *[56](SOURCES.md#F-e1ba4b224c)% of the sea has no marine observation* would name a category — marine observation — far wider than the two layers actually searched, and report the leftover after subtracting what we happened to find as though it were measured, which is the operation [RESIDUAL.md](RESIDUAL.md) is about.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-WIDER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-NAMED-CORPUS">So absence is reported here as a count over a named corpus, and the corpus is named every time.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-NAMED-CORPUS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-GAPS">**And the corpus is named together with what is missing from it.** A coverage figure has a numerator nobody can measure — the evidence that exists — so counting what we assembled gives a *lower bound on evidence* and therefore an *upper bound on absence*. That is only interpretable beside the terms we know belong in the numerator and cannot add. They are kept in `data/manual/coverage_gaps.json`, a hand-kept record, in three kinds:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-GAPS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| | source | what it would add | why we do not have it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `closed` | **PULS** | The time axis for [B1](hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") and [B2](HYPOTHESES.md "Separate stormwater"). Their discriminating test is oxygen and shore condition in the days after an overflow against that event's volume, which an annual total cannot do. | CVR-gated. Not merely a login: an access attempt with a private MitID was refused on the grounds that no CVR or VAT number attached to it was valid. Access appears to require a registered business or authority entity, so a private citizen cannot obtain it at all. |
| `closed` | **LER** | The drainage network itself, which open problem `16` says exists for exactly one Danish city and only by lucky archaeology. | Not open data. This project does not query it and no argument here depends on it. |
| `open_unassembled` | **MUNICIPAL-SPILDEVANDSPLANER** | Real catchment boundaries, which are the hard test for the inference method in X21. | None. Nobody has assembled them. Some are already in data/raw/plan_html/. |
| `open_unassembled` | **ICES-EMODNET** | Marine observation outside ODA entirely, including the cross-border series that a national extract cannot contain. | Free registration, not completed. |
| `absent` | **FISH-KILL-REGISTER** | The observable behind fiskedoed, one of the four words the public uses for the damage. | Checked and not found in open form. The surveillance is described publicly; no database is linked. |
| `closed` | **MECHANISTIC-MODEL-RUNS** | The ability to check the validation claims in GRUNDLAGET.md directly rather than through their authors' description of them. | Not published as data. The method reports are public; the runs are not. |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-GAP-CLASSES">The distinction inside that table matters as much as the table. `closed` is a gap in the world's availability; `open_unassembled` is a gap in our effort and is nobody's fault but ours; `absent` is the only one where a search was run to the end, and even that is bounded by the search.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-GAP-CLASSES "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-PULS">**PULS is the sharpest case.** It holds the per-event overflow volumes that [B1](hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") calls the single most valuable missing series — volumes that are themselves largely modelled, by this project's source register — and an access attempt with a private MitID was refused because no CVR or VAT number attached to it was valid, so this is not a login anyone has neglected to perform. Access appears to require a registered business or authority, in which case a private citizen cannot obtain it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-PULS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### How things are put into water bodies

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-ASSIGN">**Pressures are put into water bodies by nearest point on the marine boundary:** each outfall, treatment plant, aquaculture outlet, dumping ground and extraction area goes to the water body owning the nearest boundary vertex within [20](SOURCES.md#F-badc2347ae) km, searched to that distance in every direction, and to none beyond it. **Bathing stations are not placed by distance:** each goes to the water body its own record names, its `wbid`, matched exactly to the marine layer's code. Of [1,018](SOURCES.md#F-4f576f59a3) bathing stations with a classed year, [791](SOURCES.md#F-2486a832d8) are placed and [227](SOURCES.md#F-d6112048e9) left out: [103](SOURCES.md#F-348916b63a) carry a lake code, [111](SOURCES.md#F-87c9e4ad36) a coastal code the marine layer does not hold, [10](SOURCES.md#F-015f60b23b) no code, and [3](SOURCES.md#F-0438c9b8d4) a code written another way.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-ASSIGN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The record of each water body

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-RECORD">The full record for each area — every pressure, every stream with its years, and the written-out list of what cannot be modelled there — is in `data/derived/areas.json`, which `scripts/areas.py` writes locally and the repository does not ship, and drawn with its timeline on [the map](areas.html).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-RECORD "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-DOWNLOAD">A copy trimmed to what the map draws - each water body's pressures, bathing observation, streams with their years, and the reasons it cannot be modelled - is published for download as [areas.json](data/areas/areas.json).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-DOWNLOAD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-ONE-ROW">**One record, read through.** `DKCOAST2`, Roskilde Fjord, indre, is [51.8](SOURCES.md#F-721904d9f2) km² of water and one of the water bodies with a DHI statistical model. It holds [7](SOURCES.md#F-f7839bb511) bathing stations classed between [1991](SOURCES.md#F-2dd34d81e8) and [2018](SOURCES.md#F-2dd6490112); of those, the [3](SOURCES.md#F-efbc6da623) whose classes vary enough to correlate have yearly classes that correlate, pair by pair, at [0.50](SOURCES.md#F-0bd2b7349b) on average. By nearest boundary it is assigned [426](SOURCES.md#F-76b1708a27) rain-conditioned outfalls and [277,960](SOURCES.md#F-3e1b6dfe25) approved person-equivalents of treatment-plant capacity - a permitted figure, not a load. And its record gives [1](SOURCES.md#F-2c891e977a) written-out reason it cannot be modelled: it has no marine hazardous-substance monitoring point, which no water body has. Every other record in the file is built the same way.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-ONE-ROW "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The cross-water-body correlation

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-CUMHOC">The water bodies with two or more bathing stations number [65](SOURCES.md#F-d528968118), and a correlation can be computed across them - across management units, each weighted alike whatever its size or number of stations. That is not an effect of anything.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-CUMHOC "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-CUMHOC-DESIGN">This sets bathing-water quality against sewage pressure — outfall, treatment-plant and basin density per km² — because both sides of that pair exist per area. It is **cum hoc**: a correlation across places at one time, with no control for coast type, flushing, or population.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-CUMHOC-DESIGN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-CUMHOC-R">One pairing is traced end to end: the share of station-years classed below "Excellent" against approved treatment-plant capacity per km² of water body, log-scaled, **r = [+0.280](SOURCES.md#F-00f9f19776)** across the [65](SOURCES.md#F-4ea7f73896) water bodies. The other pairings, computed the same way, are in the downloadable file.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-CUMHOC-R "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-POOLING">The bathing labels change in [2011](SOURCES.md#F-1f75a18d1d): to [2010](SOURCES.md#F-58afdf5921) the file has "Good or Sufficient", from [2011](SOURCES.md#F-1f75a18d1d) "Good" and "Sufficient" apart, and the share pools both. On each period alone the same correlation is [+0.323](SOURCES.md#F-3c2fdbfc27) for [1991](SOURCES.md#F-2ba48eb7ae)–[2010](SOURCES.md#F-58afdf5921) and [+0.136](SOURCES.md#F-17faad604d) for [2011](SOURCES.md#F-1f75a18d1d)–[2018](SOURCES.md#F-3659f796ed): weaker under the newer labels.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-POOLING "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-RERUNS">How r was made - the records it rests on in their own words, each step with its code and the reason given for it, and where each branch ends - is in its "How it was made" view: open the number's menu. Reruns there each change one choice, and move r between [+0.136](SOURCES.md#F-80055aca24) and [+0.313](SOURCES.md#F-f66bd863fa).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-RERUNS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What this is not

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-W4AR-NOT">This page is not a causal model, and a water body is not the unit a cause is found in: water bodies are where responsibility sits, and the stations' co-movement draws a different map. A cause would show as stations moving together along its line; no causal line has yet been tested that way here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-W4AR-NOT "What this claim rests on")</sup>
